title: 'Pyre': An 18-Award Himalayan Love Story Arrives in Cinemas With First-Time Actors
excerpt: Vinod Kapri's Hindi drama casts two Uttarakhand villagers, aged 80 and 70, as a couple waiting 28 years for their son — and it has already collected 18 international awards, 15 of them for Best Film.
body:
• Pyre, Vinod Kapri's Hindi-language drama about an elderly couple in a Himalayan village emptying of its young, is now playing in cinemas across India after an October 30 release.
  • The film has won 18 international awards, including 15 Best Film honours, across festivals in Europe, North America and Asia.
  • Its leads, Padam Singh Kapri, 80, and Heera Devi, 70, are Uttarakhand residents who had never acted before a camera.
  • The score is by Oscar winner Mychael Danna, with a song written by Gulzar; no US release date has been announced in the coverage so far.

Some films arrive with stars. Pyre arrived with two people who had never faced a camera: Padam Singh Kapri, 80, and Heera Devi, 70, residents of Uttarakhand cast by director Vinod Kapri to play an elderly couple in the Kumaon Himalayas. The Hindi-language drama, released in cinemas across India on October 30, has already won 18 international awards, including 15 Best Film honours, at festivals across Europe, North America and Asia.

A village, a wait, and a pyre

Set in a remote village in Uttarakhand's Kumaon region, Pyre follows Padam Singh and Tulsi, an ageing couple who live together while waiting for their only son to return from the city. He has been gone 28 years. Almost all the young people have migrated in search of livelihoods, and the couple live with a fear the film takes literally: if either of them dies before their son returns, there may be nobody left in the village to carry the body to the cremation ground. So the two prepare a funeral pyre for each other near their house.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=ETmBXE66Xv4

"My encounter with 84-year-old Keshar Singh and his wife, living alone in a remote village and waiting for their only son to return to look after them in their old age, touched me deeply. The visible consequences of migration from the hills gave birth to the story of Pyre."

— Vinod Kapri, director

Kapri, a National Award-winning filmmaker who wrote, directed and produced the film, has said the project took eight years, through periods when no financier would back it — even after Oscar-winning composer Mychael Danna agreed to score it and Gulzar agreed to write a song without a fee, the Northern Gazette reported from Pithoragarh.

The festival run

Pyre premiered at the 28th Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival, where it won the Audience Award for Best Film, and went on to collect Best Film audience honours in Spain, London and Birmingham and a Best Feature Film Grand Jury Award in Stuttgart. It was also the opening film of the 16th Bengaluru International Film Festival, its Indian premiere, where it won a Jury Special Mention in the Asian Cinema Competition. The film is produced by Kapri with Suresh Joshi and Arindra Rai Chaudhuri under Bhagirathi Films and Mashakbeen Studios, and distributed by Cinépolis; ANI reported it released in Hindi and Malayalam.

How to watch

Pyre is in theatres across India now, in Hindi with Kumaoni dialect. No US theatrical or streaming release has been announced in the coverage to date, so diaspora viewers will need to wait for a distribution announcement — for a film about exactly the distance between the hills and the children who left them, that wait is part of the story.
